page.layout: One page of verse, one column; running head at top with page number at top right; no margin notes; faint show-through from the reverse page in the background, not transcribed.

main_text.p: Ast Vrae Rhodanique leues ego ftratus ad oras, Pons vbi Clufinis Cantius Allobroges Copulat; hæc Patri qui nobis otia fecit, (Otia torporis non temeranda lue) Mente, melos varium, minime variante, canendo, Vitali recreor numinis alloquio.

Alme Deus, fancta quem maiestate verendum, Ignis & auratis refplendens gloria pennis Anteit: in laudes cuius diffunditur omnis Machina, laude licet sis omni maior, & omni Eloquio; talis noftram dementia mentem Non capit, vt fperem paruo me pectore numen Claudere posse tuum: possit quod præhedere nemp. Sat vero fuerit vestigia summa sequuto, Exiles vmbras operum signare tuorum.
Tu polos præstans geminos creasti: Fulcra quo coelo minime deessent Mobili semper, variante nunquam Lege locoque.
Syderum lapsus varios & ortus Arte, (quam solers hominum fagaxque Non capit sensus) regis, & decoro Cingis amictu.
Tu parens rerum, geminos parasti Lumini currus, celeri volatu Per plagas omnes requiete nulla Orbis euntes.
Sol diem defert, gerit ima noctem: Luna, per menses properantis anni, Et leues ducit choreas reuertens Ordine certo.

page.notes: Running head and page number read as printed ("28⁵" on the scan, taken as 285). Some letters in the faint text are doubtful, notably "Anteit:in", "possit", and "hyems"; no [?] marks were placed because the scan is clear enough for most words. The line "Claudere posse tuum: possit quod præhedere nemp." is partly blurred at its end.
